title: LazyCop installs from npm in two steps, and its local server trusts only its own page

outcome: LazyCop runs only from a clone of the repo, and any web page can post to its local server.
Any request to the engine server whose Host is not 127.0.0.1 or localhost on its port gets 403.
forbid: no change to MCP tool signatures, hook input mapping or data contracts
the hook script and MCP server keep reaching the engine with no extra setup

outcome: A POST to the engine server that carries a foreign Origin, or a body that is not application/json, is refused before it is read.
forbid: the page's own POSTs (same origin) keep working

outcome: The engine reads watsonx credentials from LAZYCOP_ENV_FILE, else ~/.lazycop/.env, else the environment, never from a path relative to its own install.
forbid: without credentials LazyCop still runs and cards show Bob's own words
a credential is never written to a Bob workspace or logged

outcome: Everything the running engine serves, the logo included, lives inside the packages that ship.
npm pack of the lazycop package yields one tarball that installs globally and runs lazycop init, with no src, tests, .env or local art inside.
forbid: npm run build and the clone install in the README keep working

outcome: lazycop init warns when it runs from the npx cache, since the paths it writes would vanish with it.
lazycop init leaves .lazycop/ in the workspace .gitignore.
forbid: an existing .gitignore keeps every line it had; uninstall leaves it alone

outcome: The CLI tests hold no path from a developer's own machine.
The README installs LazyCop with npm i -g lazycop then lazycop init, and names where the watsonx key goes and that diffs go to IBM.

evidence: request-guard.ts refusal() runs first in createServer; request-guard.test.ts: Host evil.example → 403 on GET / and POST; 127.0.0.1 and localhost served. Smoke on installed tarball: Host evil.test → 403.

POST with Origin https://evil.example or another port → 403; text/plain or missing content-type → 403 before readBody; page's same-origin POST and hook/MCP origin-less JSON POSTs pass (tests + smoke: start_session over stdio worked, hook exit 0).
env.ts envFilePath(): LAZYCOP_ENV_FILE, else ~/.lazycop/.env; server.ts no longer resolves ../../../.env; existing env vars still win (loadEnvFile unchanged). env-file.test.ts 3 tests.
logo moved public/img → packages/page/img (git mv), served from pageDir; installed tarball serves /img/logo.png 200 image/png; public/ gone.

packages/cli prepack stages real copies of engine+page (their own files lists) as bundleDependencies. Tarball 7.7 MB, 59 files: 0 matches for __tests__|.ts|.map|.env|src/, no assets/*.png. npm i -g --prefix tmp + lazycop init tmp-ws wrote 4 files; engine served /, /app.js, /img/logo.png, audio. Clone path: typecheck+tests green.
cli.ts warns when inNpxCache(engine.mcpServer); gitignore.test.ts covers _npx on POSIX and Windows and a global prefix.
gitignore.ts ignoreRecords appends '.lazycop/' only if missing, only in a git repo or existing .gitignore, never rewrites; uninstall untouched. 4 tests.
install.test.ts literal /Users/truongvinh → /home/another-dev (same assertion shape); grep truongvinh packages/*/src empty.
README Install is npm i -g lazycop + lazycop init; Granite section names ~/.lazycop/.env, LAZYCOP_ENV_FILE and what is sent to watsonx; clone install moved under Development; .env.example updated.

disposition: Shipped: localhost guard (Host/Origin/content-type), ~/.lazycop/.env lookup, logo inside page package, single bundled lazycop tarball via prepack, npx-cache warning, .gitignore entry, README. Not done: npm publish (user's), license choice, engines/exports cleanup of engine index.
